trust_decision.summary: The ascii importer decides how many floats to allocate and how to index the values array from ncol*nrow read out of the untrusted file header, with no check that the payload is long enough and with the product computed in int (so it can wrap); the binary importer already carries the identical guard at the pinned commit.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary (an out-of-bounds read) and the header/negative-dimension validation in get_header lead straight to the ncol*nrow allocation and index computation in get_values; it is the only declared-dimension sizing in the ascii path and both ascii entry points funnel through it.

fix_sites.entry_point: surfio::irap::from_ascii_string and surfio::irap::from_ascii_file (Python: IrapSurface.from_ascii_string / IrapSurface.from_ascii_file), both calling get_values at :90 and :99
fix_sites.module_kind: library core - ascii import parser (public C++ header src/lib/include/irap_import.h:14-15, pybind wrappers src/pybind_module/surfio.cpp:100-109)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Export from a caller-built `irap` is a C++-only writer path (the Python bindings build the span from the numpy shape), so it can be dismissed as a caller contract, and the unguarded binary chunk count can be dismissed as format framing rather than header dimensions - and as a write where the advisory is a read.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Exporting a surface whose header dimensions exceed its values array must keep working: to_ascii_string/to_binary_buffer must serialise only the actual numpy values while the header records the declared dims (the fix's own new test builds ncol=nrow=2**12 with one value and expects to_ascii_string to succeed). A fix that validates header-vs-values in the IrapSurface constructor or in the writers breaks this. Separately, a byte-per-value guard as strict as the published `(end-start)/4` rejects valid compact ascii such as `1 2 3 4` for a 2x2 surface (7-8 payload bytes vs 4 declared values).

O6_input_shapes: ascii header whose ncol*nrow exceeds the remaining payload (truncated/short file) - the case the published guard closes

ncol*nrow whose int product wraps (e.g. 65536 x 65537 -> a small positive int), so nvalues is small while the header declares a huge grid (product now computed in size_t at src/lib/irap_import_ascii.cpp:56)
both input surfaces: memory-mapped file (from_ascii_file, src/lib/irap_import_ascii.cpp:86-93) and in-memory string_view (from_ascii_string, :95-102)
an exporter-produced string whose header declares 2**22 values while the payload holds one (the surface-object input used by the fix's own test)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The writer overloads taking `const irap&` build the value span from data.header.ncol/header.nrow over data.values.data() (surf_span at src/lib/irap_export_ascii.cpp:53 and :66; same pattern at src/lib/irap_export_binary.cpp:92 and :105), so a caller-built irap whose header dims exceed values.size() is read out of bounds; there is no header-vs-values check at the pinned commit and the published fix does not touch the writers.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: C++-only writer API whose irap argument is built by the caller, while the Python bindings derive the span from the numpy shape, so it can be called a caller contract and outside the import advisory.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package (src/lib), 3 files from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The binary import inner loop takes the write index from a per-chunk declared count without bounding it by nvalues: a chunk guard declaring 8 floats for a 1x1 header makes i run past ncol*nrow and writes values[1..7] on a size-1 vector (from_binary_buffer is reachable from Python); the header-length guard at :97-98 does not constrain per-chunk counts.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Chunk guards are format framing rather than header dimensions, the weakness is a write (CWE-787) while the advisory is a read, and the header-length guard added in the previous commit is assumed to cover the function.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, 1 file, same directory as the sibling guard

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a header-vs-values consistency check inside the `const irap&` writer overloads (also src/lib/irap_export_binary.cpp:90-94 and :103-107)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The writer is what emits a header declaring more values than the payload - the fix's own test builds exactly such a surface via to_ascii_string - so a maintainer hardening the round-trip would plausibly add the check on the writer as well.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: bound the chunk-declared value count by the remaining nvalues before writing values[ic]
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The header half of this exact guard was added one commit earlier in the same function (e009c0c 'Validate size of binary header'), leaving the chunk-count half unvalidated in the same loop.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a per-entry-point cap on ncol*nrow before allocation, or an incremental parse that grows the vector as it reads
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The two ascii entry points (file and string) share get_values and are exactly the shape the published fix changed; a maintainer could add the cap in each entry point rather than centrally.

O9_family: out-of-bounds read and over-large allocation from unvalidated file-declared grid dimensions (CWE-125, with allocation-size DoS as the observable symptom)

O10_build.toolchain: CMake >= 3.22 with scikit-build-core/ninja; pybind11 v2.13, kokkos mdspan, mio, fast_float and Catch2 are fetched by FetchContent at configure time (network at build time only); a C++20 compiler with <format>, Python development headers, numpy, pytest, pytest-memray (non-Windows), xtgeo for the binary tests
O10_build.project_tests: tests/lib/test_irap_ascii.cpp:14-28 (Catch2 round-trip of a 6000x6000 surface through to_ascii_file/from_ascii_file) and tests/python_module/test_irap_ascii.py (pytest: short file, negative dimensions, header types, 1x1/2x3 F-order, round-trip, 9-per-line). The pinned tree already contains the binary twin of the fix and its regression test: tests/python_module/test_irap_binary.py:37-44 and :103-116 assert the exact message 'ncol and nrow declared in header' for from_binary_buffer, and :119-137 covers negative dims; the fix adds the same 10 MB pytest-memray test to the ascii file.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Copy the published two-line `(end-start)/4` guard (in practice, the identical guard and its test already visible in get_values_binary and tests/python_module/test_irap_binary.py at the pinned commit) into get_values, widen ncol/nrow to size_t, and stop - leaving the writer overloads and the binary chunk count unguarded, while the byte-per-value rule also rejects valid compact ascii.

out_of_scope_notes: src/lib/include/irap_import.h:10-12 names the parameters (idx, nrow, ncol) while both call sites pass (i, ncol, nrow); the formula is consistent with the call sites, so this is a naming trap rather than a defect and is outside this advisory.
unverified: Whether fix_commits is meant to exclude the parent commit e009c0c ('Validate size of binary header'): that commit is the same security change and is already in the pinned tree with the identical guard (src/lib/irap_import_binary.cpp:97-98), the identical error message and its regression test (tests/python_module/test_irap_binary.py:103-116), which makes the ascii fix a one-line copy away; the candidate metadata lists only 1619750b.

Whether the export-from-irap O8 route is reachable from the hidden behavioural tests: it is C++-only because the Python bindings use make_surf_span over the numpy shape, so it would need a ctest/C++ test rather than a Python test.

Whether the two tests the fix diff modifies (test_short_files_result_in_value_error, test_non_floats_result_in_domain_error), which do exist at the pinned commit, should count as regression_tests_in_pinned_commit; the fix's actual new regression test (10 MB memray test) is absent from the pinned tree, and the binary twin test is an older test for the same area, so the flag was left out.

Whether hidden tests exercise compact ascii value tokens (e.g. `1 2 3 4` for a 2x2 surface): by arithmetic from src/lib/irap_import_ascii.cpp:56 and fix.diff:16 the published `(end-start)/4` guard rejects them, but this was not run.
Repository size in MB was not measured (no shell); the whole tree is about 25 source/test files of a few hundred lines each, so tiny_repo is judged from the directory listing.
